extra_misconceptions.fact: Metal stops glowing red below about 900 degrees Fahrenheit, so dark metal can still cause severe third-degree burns on contact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Black iron or copper that shows no red glow on the anvil is cool enough to pick up with bare hands.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rotating machinery can snag a glove and pull your hand into the spindle or wheel, so keep hands bare near spinning tools.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Thick leather work gloves should always be worn while operating a drill press or powered bench grinder.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water trapped beneath molten metal flashes instantly into steam and causes a violent explosion that scatters liquid metal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Throwing water onto a crucible of molten aluminum or bronze is the fastest way to cool a spill.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Metalwork requires ANSI Z87.1 rated safety glasses or a face shield with side protection to stop high-velocity metal shards.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard prescription eyeglasses provide sufficient impact protection when chiseling, peening, or shearing sheet metal.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to wear synthetic fleece or loose gloves near a hot forge or spinning drill press?
What happens to galvanized zinc coatings when heated in a forge or crucible without proper ventilation?
Where should a Scout position the quench bucket and Class ABC fire extinguisher before lighting a forge?
Which physical indicator warns you that a freshly quenched or newly sheared piece of metal is still hazardous?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ferrous means the alloy contains iron, and nickel-rich 300-series austenitic stainless steels are ferrous yet non-magnetic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every ferrous alloy will stick strongly to a permanent magnet during a workshop sorting test.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Traditional bronze combines copper with tin, whereas brass is a distinct nonferrous alloy made by combining copper with zinc.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bronze and brass are two names for the same ancient copper alloy used before the Iron Age.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Native metals occur in nature in their pure metallic state and can be shaped by cold hammering without smelting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Native metals like copper, gold, and silver must be smelted from oxide ore before they exist in metallic form.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Malleability is a metal's ability to deform under compressive hammering or rolling, while ductility measures tensile stretching.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Malleability measures how easily a metal wire can be stretched under tension without snapping.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the melting point and hardness of pure copper when a metallurgist alloys it with tin to make bronze?
Which physical indicator during a magnet or grinder spark test distinguishes high-carbon steel from nonferrous brass?
Under what condition does an austenitic stainless steel alloy remain non-magnetic despite being a ferrous metal?
What elemental difference separates ancient bronze from brass when you log their nonferrous base metal compositions?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Copper and brass only harden through cold mechanical working, and heating them followed by water quenching anneals them soft.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Quenching red-hot sheet copper or brass in cold water hardens the metal just like quenching high-carbon tool steel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fully quenched high-carbon steel is glass-brittle and will shatter on impact unless reheated to a straw or purple temper color.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High-carbon steel is ready to use as a striking tool immediately after quenching from critical red heat in water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must sand or file the hardened steel bright and clean before tempering so the thin oxide color bands are clearly visible.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Temper colors on heated steel appear even if the metal surface is covered in black forge scale and oil.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Permanent deformation and work-hardening occur only after applied force exceeds the metal's yield point into plastic deformation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bending a metal strip within its elastic range permanently alters its shape and work-hardens the grain boundaries.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the crystal grain structure along the bend line when you heavily peen 26-gauge copper or brass?
Why does quenching red-hot copper in water anneal and soften it while quenching red-hot high-carbon steel makes it brittle?
Which oxide temper color on polished steel indicates the right hardness and toughness balance for a cold chisel?
What tactile change in resistance confirms you have exceeded the yield point when unbending your annealed copper strip?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many skilled metalworking careers use paid union apprenticeships, trade school programs, and AWS or NIMS industry certifications.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year university degree in engineering is required before entering any high-paying career in modern metalworking.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Welding certifications are qualified for specific processes, metal thicknesses, and positions, and require periodic testing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing a single visual weld inspection certifies a welder for all metals, joint positions, and structural codes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: CNC machinists must still select cutting speeds, tooling, and coolant based on how each alloy work-hardens and conducts heat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Computer numerical control automation has eliminated the need for human machinists to understand metallurgy and tool feeds.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Blacksmiths shape heated steel by hammer and eye on an anvil, while aerospace foundries cast alloys using X-ray inspection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Farriers and ornamental blacksmiths use the exact same tooling, furnaces, and quality metrics as aerospace foundry technicians.

extra_socratic_questions: What industry certification confirms a structural welder or CNC machinist meets national quality and safety standards?
Which personal tool expenses and apprenticeship hours must a candidate log before qualifying as a journeyman sheet metal worker?
Where should a Scout position himself during a commercial foundry or machine shop tour to observe operations safely?
What distinguishes the daily production tolerances of an industrial tool-and-die maker from those of an artistic blacksmith?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Closing snips completely to the tips leaves tiny sharp burrs and nicks, so stop each cut slightly short of the blade tips.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting all the way to the tip of tin snips on every stroke produces the cleanest, smoothest edge on sheet metal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Solder only wets and bonds to oxide-free metal that has been mechanically cleaned, coated with flux, and heated evenly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Solder will flow into a dirty sheet metal or silver joint as long as you hold the soldering iron on the seam long enough.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The runner channels molten metal into the mold cavity, while the riser holds a reservoir of liquid metal to feed shrinkage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: In sand casting, the runner and the riser perform the exact same job of venting trapped air out of the mold cavity.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drawing out lengthens and thins the metal along its axis, whereas upsetting drives the hot bar back on itself to thicken it.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drawing out hot iron on the anvil makes the workpiece shorter and thicker at the hammered section.

extra_socratic_questions: What layout allowance must you add to your flat sheet metal sketch dimensions when folding a hem or locked seam?
Which aviation snip color code is designed for cutting straight lines or wide curves without kinking the sheet edge?
Why is it dangerous to strike a hardened steel hammer face directly against the hardened face of an anvil or stake?
What happens to a sand casting if the founder omits the riser or packs damp molding sand without vent channels?
